findings.reason: a node implementing §2 verbatim writes a test whose first case cannot pass, and the only way to green it is to substitute a different goal input, which is exactly the class of silent input substitution the case exists to prevent.
findings.text: §2's first done-when case specifies the goal `read the config; reload the lane` as an entry the node contract refuses, but `_deliverable_conjunction` (reckon/crew/node.py:252) refuses a separator only when the following clause opens with a verb in `_DELIVERABLE_ACTIONS` (node.py:79-104), which contains neither `read` nor `reload` — running the shipped function on that exact string returns None, and `validate_node` on a node carrying it reports no `single-goal` finding (control: `read the config; run the lane` returns `;`), so the well-formed refusal the case asserts never happens and the batch would store the entry
